dct_description_sm: The long-term goal of our research is to improve our understanding of the linkages between mercury sources and pathways of mercury methylation, which ultimately give rise to the relatively high levels in Arctic marine food webs. Ultimately, we envision these data being used together with data from other ongoing studies and community knowledge to develop  a practical Hg monitoring strategy for Canada's Arctic waters. Specifically, the goals of the project reported here, are: i) to assess the spatial patterns of Mercury (Hg) and Methylmercury (MeHg) distribution along Canada's Arctic margin, for comparison to geographic trends identified in the marine food web, and ii) to improve our understanding of the MeHg sources and production pathways in the Arctic Ocean along the Canadian Arctic margin by examining the inter-relationships between Hg, MeHg, organic carbon and other geochemical properties of the sediments.
dct_title_s: Methylmercury Pathways in the Water Column and Sediments along Canada's Arctic Margin
